ideas: Higher turnout makes results more representative
Freedom includes the right not to vote
Forced voters may choose randomly or carelessly

phrases.meaning: have to pay money as punishment

model: I'm in favour of compulsory voting, although I understand why many people disagree. My main reason is that it makes results more representative. When voter turnout is low, elections are usually decided by older or wealthier people, whereas if everyone votes, the government has to represent the whole population. Australia is a good example. Voting has been compulsory there since the 1920s, people who don't vote can be fined, and turnout is usually around ninety percent. It also treats voting as a civic duty, like paying taxes, so young people get used to having a say in politics. Some colleagues of mine argue that it takes away freedom of choice, and I think that's a fair point. They also worry that people who are forced to vote won't make an informed decision. Despite these concerns, I think the benefits are bigger. And if someone really doesn't like any candidate, they can still spoil their ballot, so nobody is actually forced to support anyone.
